title: Working Memory
content_html:
Working Memory

Architecture & Capacity

Architecture (Multicomponent Model)

Central Executive — attentional control: selection, shifting, inhibition; minimal storage.

Phonological Loop — verbal/auditory buffer with articulatory rehearsal (≈2 s of speech).

Visuospatial Sketchpad — visual and spatial buffer for images, locations, features.

Episodic Buffer — limited-capacity multimodal workspace that binds across buffers and long-term memory into a unified “episode”.

Model origins and update adding the episodic buffer in 2000; integrative role emphasized in 2012 review.

Capacity & Chunking

Modern consensus: ≈ 3–4 chunks in the focus of attention (Cowan).

Visual WM: often ≈3–4 simple objects/features (Luck & Vogel and subsequent work).

Classic heuristic: 7±2 (Miller), largely superseded for WM proper by the 3–4 estimate.

Chunking & rehearsal can raise effective span by recoding and refreshing.

Multicomponent working memory with domain-specific buffers coordinated by a central executive; an episodic buffer integrates across stores and links to long-term memory. Capacity annotations reflect typical contemporary estimates:

Design Cues

  • Present information in separate channels (verbal + visual) to leverage domain-specific buffers.
  • Target 3–4 integrated units at a time; scaffold chunking with structure and prior knowledge.
  • Use brief rehearsal opportunities (self-explanation, recitation) to refresh fragile traces.
  • When integration across sources is needed, provide an “episode” scaffold (summary frame or diagram) to offload binding demands.
